name: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc.

profile.description: Howard Hughes Holdings owns master planned communities (Summerlin, Bridgeland), operating assets and condominium developments, and is being transformed by Pershing Square into a Berkshire-style holding company built around Vantage insurance. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.12B (+330% YoY) on condo closings, Q1 MPC EBT rose 33% to $84.4M, and 2026 condo revenue is guided to $720-750M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track record 2: strategic transformation into a permanent-capital holding company led by Pershing Square with Vantage insurer at its center [2]. Share 1: leading MPC land seller in Summerlin and Bridgeland (MPC EBT +33%) [1]. Pipeline 2: 2026 guidance of $720-750M condo revenue and $279-290M operating asset NOI [1]. No AI deployment (0) or R&D (0).

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission floor 2: place-making for communities, clear but not distinctive [1]. Community 1: general community development at scale. Insider conviction 2: Executive Chairman Bill Ackman's Pershing Square has repeatedly increased its stake, a roughly $900M commitment [2]; no retention data.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated (growth weights, 10 units): D/E 135% = 0.72; ROE 7.5% = 0.50 (2x); revenue YoY 330% = 1.0; forward P/E 70 = 0.0; margin 12.3% = 0.62; 5yr CAGR and PEG unavailable. Weighted 3.33/6 = 5.5, rounded to 6.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: Master planned communities, condos and operating assets are physical-world businesses with no AI substitution risk; the filings flag only execution risk of adopting AI too slowly versus competitors [2]. No AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Controlled by Pershing Square with a mandate to build a perpetual holding company; long-term capital orientation but quarterly lumpiness and transition risk.

just_cause.analysis: Building enduring communities and a permanent-capital compounder is a distinctive long-horizon goal, but the holding-company identity is only 18 months old [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Management team under CEO David O'Reilly was retained through the Pershing transition; no culture survey data [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Capital allocation framed around Buffett-style winning; no evidence of worthy-rival mindset.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Transforming a real estate developer into a Berkshire-style insurance-led holding company is a fundamental reinvention [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Plans to sell up to $4B of real estate to fund insurance acquisitions despite near-term earnings dilution [2].

investment_thesis: Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.12B (+330%) on condo closings, MPC EBT grew 33% in Q1 to $84.4M, and 2026 NOI guidance is $279-290M [1]. Pershing Square's control and plan to redeploy real estate cash into Vantage insurance could compound book value like early Berkshire [2].
thesis_continued: Forward P/E is 70x, D/E is 135%, ROE is only 7.5%, and Q1 net income fell 25% to $8.7M on higher interest costs [1]. Revenue is lumpy from condo closings, the insurance pivot is unproven, and the stock already reflects the Ackman premium.
key_catalysts: Execution of $720-750M condo closings and MPC land sales
Vantage insurance acquisitions funded by asset sales of up to $4B
key_risks: Lumpy condo revenue and elevated interest costs
Unproven insurance operating model under holding company transition
sources: Howard Hughes Holdings Q1 and Q2 2026 Earnings Releases, SEC 8-K and Simply Wall St, 2026
Pershing Square and Howard Hughes transformation, CoStar/Commercial Property Executive/Hedgeweek, 2025-2026
